body.statement: On \(\mathfrak M_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\), the ordinary interval \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm W}\), computed from outcomes observed through \(H_T=T+\Delta_T\), is uniformly asymptotically honest if and only if \(T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\to0\). If this product converges to a positive finite constant, a compatible hidden-sign family has a nonzero shifted-Gaussian limit and ordinary-Wald undercoverage; if it diverges, ordinary-Wald coverage tends to zero along a compatible family. At \(\Delta_T=0\), ordinary Wald is uniformly honest exactly when \(\beta>q\).
body.justification: Because follow-up changes both truncation ages and the observations entering the statistic, the uniform if-and-only-if criterion separates a class-wide ordinary-Wald guarantee, a class-wide tail-padding requirement, and sufficient endpoint follow-up.
body.gap: Classical delayed urn inference gives usual asymptotics, and delayed CARA theory assumes ignorable delays; neither characterizes the informative-tail follow-up boundary.
body.consumer: A protocol can select no pad, a bias-aware pad, or additional follow-up from the prespecified exploration and endpoint-tail exponents.
